tasks.spec:
You are a read-only diagnosis scout. Your working directory contains ./packet/ — a frozen evidence snapshot of the Loop Factory podcast department, a watchdog/manager that governs podcast automation loops. You have NO network and NO filesystem beyond this directory. You must not modify, delete, or add anything under ./packet (its hashes are verified after you finish). Your only deliverable is ./report.md.

THE PROBLEM: the department's manager cycle is dead while its sensor is alive. Evidence already in the packet: packet/state/STATE.json shows last_run_at advancing (2026-08-05T19:00Z, epoch 1719) while last_cycle_at is frozen at 2026-08-03T02:30:01Z; packet/state/heartbeats-tail.jsonl stops at epoch 1587, ts 2026-08-03T02:30Z, while packet/state/runs-tail.jsonl continues past epoch 1715; packet/estate-STATE.json carries an open 'dead_manager' breach finding for podcast. The orchestrator is packet/runtime/podcast_daily.sh, launched by the systemd units in packet/units/ (journal excerpt since Aug 2: packet/journal-podcast-loop.txt). The python runtime nodes it drives are in packet/runtime/.

YOUR JOB: read the orchestrator and the journal, find WHERE the cycle path stopped producing heartbeats and last_cycle_at updates after 2026-08-03T02:30Z while the sense path kept running, and name the mechanism. First trace which stage of podcast_daily.sh (or which runtime node it calls) writes last_cycle_at and appends heartbeats — follow the code in packet/runtime/. Then find in packet/journal-podcast-loop.txt or the state files why that stage stopped being reached or stopped succeeding at that timestamp.

OUTPUT CONTRACT — write ./report.md with exactly these sections:
# Manager Deadstall Diagnosis
## Root cause
One paragraph. Must include a line starting exactly 'ROOT CAUSE:' naming the mechanism, plus file:line references into packet/ for the code path.
## Evidence chain
Numbered steps from symptom to cause. Include at least 3 lines starting exactly 'QUOTE: ' — each followed by ONE line copied byte-for-byte from a packet file (a journal line, a state line, or a code line), then the packet-relative path in parentheses, e.g.: QUOTE: some exact line here (packet/journal-podcast-loop.txt). The checker greps every QUOTE against the named file and FAILS the report if it is not a verbatim substring.
## What still works
Why sensing / last_run_at keeps advancing, with file:line.
## Proposed minimal fix
A line starting exactly 'PROPOSED FIX:' plus at most 10 lines describing the smallest change or operator action that restarts manager cycles, and which file/timestamp advancing would prove the fix worked.
## Confidence and unknowns
What the packet cannot prove. Do not guess — mark unknowns as unknowns and name the exact file that would settle each one.

HARD RULES: analysis only; never invent file contents; every claim about code or logs must cite a packet path; cite at least 4 packet/ paths across the report; if the packet lacks the decisive evidence, say exactly which file would settle it instead of speculating.
tasks.verified: report.md exists with all required sections, a non-empty ROOT CAUSE and PROPOSED FIX line, >=4 packet path citations, >=3 verbatim quotes that grep-match their cited packet files, and the packet sha manifest shows the scout modified nothing.

tasks.spec:
You are a read-only verification scout. Your working directory contains ./packet/ — a frozen snapshot of the two escalation-card systems that buzz the owner's phone with Approve/Respond buttons. You have NO network and NO filesystem beyond this directory. Never modify anything under ./packet (hashes are verified after you finish). Your only deliverable is ./report.md.

THE QUESTION: do BOTH card creators record their cards in the ONE ledger that the hourly re-escalation job reads, so every unanswered card gets re-armed on the owner's phone — or is there a split brain where some cards are created but never re-armed?

System A (OBE loop escalations): packet/obe_escalation_card.py creates Linear cards for podcast loop escalations, using packet/obe_tg_notify.py as its Telegram transport.
System B (factory mailroom): packet/factory/outbox_push.py, packet/factory/outbox_listen.py, and packet/factory/mailroom_registry.py create and track cards from department outbox files according to the config packet/outbox_push.yaml.
Re-arm leg: packet/factory/reescalate.py runs hourly (systemd units in packet/units/) against the ledger_file named in packet/outbox_push.yaml. A recent excerpt of that ledger is packet/card-ledger-tail.jsonl. NOTE: one row in the excerpt is tagged 'split-brain-ledger-migration-2026-08-05' — a ledger unification was in progress on Aug 5; your job is to verify from the code whether it is COMPLETE in this snapshot, not to assume either way.

VERIFY, with file:line evidence for each: (1) where System A records its created cards — the same ledger file, a different file, or nowhere; (2) whether reescalate.py's row-selection logic (which rows count as open/unanswered — field names, status vocabulary, kind values) covers rows as System A writes them; (3) which watches/departments feed System B per packet/outbox_push.yaml, and whether the OBE podcast loop lane is among them; (4) every gap that would leave an unanswered card un-re-armed.

OUTPUT CONTRACT — write ./report.md with exactly these sections:
# Single Ledger Verification
## Verdict
A line that is exactly 'SINGLE_LEDGER: yes' or 'SINGLE_LEDGER: no', then one paragraph of justification.
## Writers
For each system: file:line of every ledger write, or 'writes nowhere' with the evidence.
## Re-arm coverage
How reescalate.py selects rows; whether System A's rows match that selection; cite at least 2 real card identifiers (ANK-<number>) from packet/card-ledger-tail.jsonl as worked examples of rows that would or would not be re-armed.
## Gaps
Numbered; each with file:line and the concrete consequence. This section may be empty only if the verdict is SINGLE_LEDGER: yes.
## Evidence quotes
At least 3 lines starting exactly 'QUOTE: ' — each ONE line copied byte-for-byte from a packet file, then the packet-relative path in parentheses, e.g.: QUOTE: exact line (packet/factory/reescalate.py). The checker greps every QUOTE against the named file and FAILS on any mismatch.

HARD RULES: analysis only; never invent file or code contents; every claim cites a packet path; treat the Telegram sender scripts as opaque transports (they are deliberately not in the packet); mark unknowns as unknowns and name the file that would settle each.
tasks.verified: report.md exists with all required sections, exactly one strict SINGLE_LEDGER verdict line, >=2 cited ANK card ids that really occur in the ledger excerpt, >=3 verbatim quotes that grep-match their cited packet files, and the packet sha manifest shows the scout modified nothing.
